note: HTTP Response Headers stores each header as a `response_header` config entity (http_response_headers.response_header.<id>) with fields name (actual HTTP header), value, status, visibility (core condition plugins). The AddHTTPHeaders subscriber (KernelEvents::RESPONSE priority -100) applies enabled entities; an EMPTY value removes that header. Managed at /admin/config/system/response-headers. Ships 10 optional default headers incl. x_frame_options=SAMEORIGIN. Medium cases read back a known custom entity's value/status. Hard cases create custom entities keyed by name+value (X-Frame-Options: DENY; X-Robots-Tag: noindex); resets delete only those specific attempts, never the shipped defaults, so verify fails on empty state and the shared site is left clean.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site with http_response_headers enabled, where do I go to add a custom HTTP response header (like X-Frame-Options: DENY), and what config entity type stores it?
evals.expected_output: Go to Configuration > System > HTTP Response Headers (/admin/config/system/response-headers, route entity.response_header.collection) and add a header. Each header is a `response_header` config entity (http_response_headers.response_header.<id>) with a name (the HTTP header), value, status and optional visibility conditions.

evals.prompt: Using the http_response_headers module, how do I make Drupal stop sending a header such as X-Powered-By?
evals.expected_output: Create/enable a response_header entity whose name is X-Powered-By and whose value is empty. The AddHTTPHeaders response subscriber removes any header whose configured value is empty (this is how the shipped x_powered_by and x_generator defaults strip those headers).

evals.prompt: What fields does a response_header config entity in the http_response_headers module have, and when in the request lifecycle are the headers applied?
evals.expected_output: Fields: id, label, description, name (the actual HTTP header), value, status (enabled), and visibility (core condition plugins evaluated with AND). The AddHTTPHeaders event subscriber applies enabled entities on KernelEvents::RESPONSE at priority -100 (empty value removes the header).

evals.prompt: This site has an http_response_headers configuration whose HTTP header name is 'X-Custom-Test'. Inspect the live configuration and tell me what value that header is set to.
evals.expected_output: The response_header entity hrh_med_value sets X-Custom-Test to 'medium-value' (name=X-Custom-Test, value=medium-value, status=true).

evals.prompt: There is an http_response_headers configuration on this site for the header 'X-Disabled-Test'. Inspect it and state whether that header is currently being sent (enabled) or not.
evals.expected_output: It is disabled — the response_header entity hrh_med_disabled (name X-Disabled-Test) has status=false, so the header is not sent.

evals.prompt: I want to stop other websites from being able to embed my site inside a frame or iframe at all. Use the HTTP Response Headers module to send X-Frame-Options with the value DENY, and apply it to the site.
evals.expected_output: Create (or reconfigure) an enabled response_header config entity with name 'X-Frame-Options' and value 'DENY' so the site responds with X-Frame-Options: DENY.

evals.prompt: Using the http_response_headers module, configure the site to send the response header 'X-Robots-Tag: noindex' and apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create an enabled response_header config entity with name 'X-Robots-Tag' and value 'noindex' (http_response_headers.response_header.<id>), so the site sends X-Robots-Tag: noindex.
